title: Lamella Clarifier

introduction.definition: A lamella clarifier uses a pack of inclined plates (≈ 55–60°) spaced a few centimetres apart. Each plate adds settling area, so particles settle only a short distance before sliding down the plate into the sludge hopper, while clear water rises between the plates to collection launders. It needs a fraction of the footprint of a conventional clarifier.
applications: Mine water, filter backwash recovery and industrial effluents
key_points: Projected plate area does the settling

pressure.title: Projected plate area does the work
pressure.description: Settling depends on surface area. Each inclined plate adds its horizontal projected area, so a lamella clarifier provides many times the settling area of a conventional clarifier of the same footprint. Particles only fall a few centimetres to the plate, then slide down into the hopper while clarified water flows up between the plates to the launders.

foundation: Reinforced-concrete tank on prepared ground; watertightness test before backfill; allow for buoyancy when empty (groundwater).
alignment: Weirs and launders levelled to a few millimetres so overflow is even; drive/bridge centred and level.
piping: Inlet arranged to spread flow without short-circuiting; sludge lines with flushing points; overflow and drain to a safe place.
commissioning: Fill with clean water, check for leaks; run mechanisms empty and with water; start chemical dosing and tune by jar tests.

routine.task: Check outlet turbidity and sludge level.

lubrication: No routine lubrication on static parts; lubricate valve stems and actuators per maker.

safety: Plate packs are heavy — use lifting gear; confined spaces in hoppers.

video_tutorials.title: Lamella Clarifier — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Lamella Clarifier.
A lamella clarifier uses a pack of inclined plates (≈ 55–60°) spaced a few centimetres apart.
Each plate adds settling area, so particles settle only a short distance before sliding down the plate into the sludge hopper, while clear water rises between the plates to collection launders.
It needs a fraction of the footprint of a conventional clarifier.
Typical applications include compact water and wastewater clarification; mine water, filter backwash recovery and industrial effluents.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Lamella Clarifier — Operation

script.narration: How the Lamella Clarifier works.
Flocculated water enters the inlet channel.
It turns under the plate pack and rises between the plates.
Particles settle on the plates and slide down to the hopper.
Clear water overflows the launders.
Sludge is drawn from the hopper.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Settling depends on surface area.

video_tutorials.title: Lamella Clarifier — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Lamella Clarifier.
Check outlet turbidity and sludge level.
Hose down plates; clean launders.
Remove plates; inspect supports.
Watch for plate fouling: uneven flow, turbidity rise. Common cause: biological growth, scale.
Watch for sludge carry-over: turbid launders. Common cause: hopper full.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
